field_notes.deck_order_rank: Renamed from 'frequency_rank' (2026-07-20, item 40): the value is the card's position in the deck (= lesson_order), NOT a corpus frequency rank. Do not read it as frequency; populate a real frequency source before renaming back.
field_notes.secondary_readings: Jouyo readings intentionally DEMOTED off the card face (item 19): they exist and are dictionary-valid, but are not shown with equal prominence to the N4-target readings in on/kun. on/kun = N4-target/common; secondary_readings = demoted; complete jouyo = the union (item 13).
field_notes.origin_disputed: True where the card's Type is tagged '(disputed)'; the competing scholarly views are named in the Excel Confidence column (the dispute record; item 45).
field_notes.mnemonic_not_etymology: True where the drawn scene is a labelled MEMORY DEVICE (borrowed / 仮借 / folk-corrected / shinjitai mnemonic), i.e. pedagogically useful but not the literal historical origin (item 46). Derived from the Excel Origin/Scene text.
field_notes.source_of_truth: Readings + meanings are BUILT from KnowledgeBank/kanji_n4.md via tools/build_data.py (now merge-preserving - item 42). Examples/notes/flags/secondary_readings are hand-authored here and preserved across rebuilds. The card etymology/type/source/confidence live in the Excel (col 6 Origin, col 13 Source, col 14 Confidence). Source-policy override rule (item 44): modern scholarship (Wiktionary/說文/OC/KANJIDIC2/常用漢字表) decides Type + component roles; kanjiportraits is the memory-hook IMAGERY source only, never the authority for 六書 or semantic/phonetic roles.
field_notes.n4_kanji_readings_json: Holds BOTH n5_prerequisite and core_n4 kanji, distinguished by each entry's `tier` field (item 39 - not renamed to avoid breaking the app/build that read it by name; the tier field already separates the two sets).
field_notes.recognition_priority_REMOVED: Removed 2026-07-20 (recheck item 33): it was a coarse deck-position tier, not an evidence-based instructional priority, and the app does not read it. Re-introduce only if computed from a documented frequency + pedagogy model.
field_notes.reading_format_n5_vs_n4: n4_kanji_readings.json stores N5-prerequisite on-readings in HIRAGANA and core-N4 on-readings in KATAKANA (different build sources). The file is app-consumed (js/furigana.js popover + sw.js cache); normalizing N5->katakana is DEFERRED pending a popover render-check, to avoid changing app-consumed data blind (recheck item 34).
field_notes.readings_file_name: n4_kanji_readings.json holds BOTH n5_prerequisite and core_n4 (per-entry `tier`); NOT renamed - it is read by name by js/furigana.js and cached by sw.js, so a rename needs coordinated app + service-worker-cache changes (deferred; recheck item 35).
field_notes.excel_structured_metadata: The Excel now carries normalized columns 19 'Confidence level' (High/Medium/Low/Disputed) + 20 'Source authority' + 21 'Source access', derived from the prose Confidence (col 14) and Source (col 13); the prose stays the full reason/locator (recheck items 36/37). Full per-cell verification-date/locator/alternate structuring is deferred - that info lives in the prose + readme R27/R47.
field_notes.confidence_level_normalized: Excel col 19: controlled High/Medium/Low/Disputed; Disputed iff origin_disputed (enforced by verify_kanji_data check 12). The prose reason stays in col 14.
field_notes.grammar_note: Per-example optional field: conjugation guidance (e.g. 'u-verb that looks like a ru-verb') lives HERE, never inside the gloss (enforced by check 13).

entries.notes: A crowd squeezed under one roof, all speaking with one mouth, says the SAME thing.
A hand busy with a tool, with a job to handle: a THING that needs doing.
It's a picture of a NOSE; 'oneself' just borrowed its sound. (Japanese do point at their own nose for 'me' - a handy memory aid.)
A taut bow lets its arrow fly off - it SETS OFF and starts.
Twigs crackle and spark in a little stove; that shape was borrowed to mean the ONE who does it - someone.
Soil on the left with a long curling tail beside it: the GROUND we stand on.
Heaps of work piled high on a big wooden stand: that is your BUSINESS and WORK.
A signpost with one arm pointing the WAY to go.
A flat, prepared patch of ground (土) is the PLACE where things happen; 昜 gives only the sound.
Two hands reach into the gate and lift the bar, so it swings OPEN.
The mouth (口) is what asks; the gate 門 only gives the sound - so, to ASK.
One person steps in to take another's place and TAKE A TURN.
At DAWN the sun is rising while the moon still lingers - their two lights together = BRIGHT. (Both the sun+moon and the older window+moon forms are ancient; 說文's standard is the window form.)
It takes real strength to MOVE something heavy.
A tall tower raised on a high hill: that grew into the big CAPITAL city.
A road runs straight through, so you can PASS along it.
Put everything neatly in its right place, in good order: that is REASON and sense.
A person plus their main trunk makes the whole BODY.
One flame on top of the lamp stand is the MAIN one, the master.
A big head bends over the page to think up the TOPIC.
What your heart wants to say, put into words: that is your IDEA, what you mean.
It's a flower's calyx; the shape was simply borrowed to mean NO / not.
A person cuts and shapes the wood to MAKE something.
A strong bucket you pick up and USE for a job.
A hand measures the same thing again and again: each measure is one DEGREE, one time.
The bug radical (虫) is the real part - it was a grain-weevil; 'strong' only borrowed the sound.
Split it open and share with everyone: that is PUBLIC.

examples.gloss: to hold (in one's hand); to take

entries.notes: The hand on the left reaches out to grip and HOLD on tight.
Wide open land stretching past the village: a FIELD.
Stand at one point and count everything FROM there onward.
Your head on top and your heart below work together when you THINK.
The roof (宀) makes it a home; the pig-part gives only the sound - so, HOUSE.
One family growing on and on, parents to children: the WORLD through its many ages.
Two cuts of meat stacked one on another - a generous pile means MANY.
Stop with your feet right on the line: that is CORRECT.
A big walled building up on the hill, like a hospital: a large INSTITUTION.
A little heart with its three beats: your HEART and mind.
Fields split into zones by fences: each one a WORLD with its border.
An elder guides a child with a gentle tap to help them learn: to TEACH.
Strokes crossed like a woven pattern make WRITING.
A person with a big head drawn up top: the head is the start, the ORIGIN of it all.
A bundle stacked up and pressed down feels HEAVY.
Just a short walk down the road: that is NEAR.

examples.gloss: way of thinking; point of view

entries.notes: A wise elder bends down to think hard and CONSIDER.
A neat frame drawn around a field: a PICTURE.
Water on the left as far as you can see: the wide SEA.
Put your goods OUT on the stand for everyone to buy: that is to SELL.

examples.grammar_note: u-verb (Group 1) that looks like a ru-verb (Group 2)

entries.notes: Memory hook: answer as fast and straight as an arrow because you KNOW it. (In the 形声 reading 矢 is the SOUND-part, not 'arrow-speed'; 說文 reads it 会意.)
Birds GATHER together on one tree.
A knife slices it apart, to SEPARATE into pieces.
A cow and other goods: any THING you can name.

examples.gloss: to use; to make use of

entries.notes: Send a person off to do a job: to USE them.
Three little boxes stacked on the shelf: GOODS for sale.
Use words and numbers to COUNT and plan.
A person kneels quietly beside the old bones: the end of life.
One prize cow kept apart from the herd: the SPECIAL one.

examples.gloss: beginning of the year; new year

entries.notes: 女 (woman) carries the meaning; 台 gives only the sound. Memory image only: a mother starting a new life = the BEGINNING.
The sun climbs through the grass while the moon still hangs: MORNING.
A covered cart rolls down the road to CARRY the load.

examples.gloss: to end; to come to an end

entries.notes: A cord knotted at both ends marks where the thread (糸) runs out - the END; 冬 gives only the sound.
A small block on a firm base makes a STAND.
entries.display_meaning: pedestal; a stand; counter for machines

entries.notes: A roof opening out over the land: a WIDE, roomy space.
A person settles down by the steady lamp to LIVE there.
A person dancing with streamers; the shape was borrowed to mean NOTHING (the 'dance' sense moved to 舞).
A precious pot filled right to the brim - full, so genuine and TRUE.
The meat (肉) is the thing you own; the hand 又 gives only the sound - so, to HAVE.
A few tiny bits with one slice taken off: only a LITTLE.

examples.gloss: old-town district; the traditional part of a city

entries.notes: Fields with a few buildings beside them: a small TOWN.
Scoop out rice to measure the MATERIALS you need.
A carpenter's tool of two bars and a post: CRAFT and building.

examples.gloss: to be erected; to be built

entries.notes: Stand it up straight and tall, piece by piece: to BUILD.
心 (heart) carries the meaning; 及 gives the sound. Memory hook: a hand chasing from behind + a racing heart = HURRY.
One footprint planted firmly on the spot: STOP right here.
Set it on the road and wave it off: to SEND it away.
A blade chops down on the right to CUT it.
The cart wheel spins around, so things TURN and roll.
Rub it on a flat stone over and over to POLISH and study.
穴 (cave/hole) carries the meaning; 九 gives the sound. Memory hook: dig deep into a winding cave to the end = RESEARCH.
Strings stretched across a wooden frame, played for MUSIC and fun (the top element is debated).
Spring up off the ground and start running: WAKE UP.
Memory device: picture grass/sprigs (艹) settling and sticking onto a spot; 者 gives only the sound. 着 is a later split of 著 - the attach/wear/arrive senses are the word's, not built from 艹.
A person lies in bed under the sick roof: that is ILLNESS.
Check it carefully to see if it is the real, solid thing inside: that is its QUALITY.
Stand on the path and WAIT for your turn.

examples.gloss: to try (out); to have a try (at)

entries.notes: Say the words and follow the steps to TRY it out.
One flag and a shared bundle of arrows bring the whole FAMILY together.
A shiny metal, not gold but SILVER.
One telling: the sun sits low at first light = EARLY. (The origin is genuinely disputed.)

examples.gloss: to be reflected; to appear on a screen

entries.notes: Sunlight hits the middle and bounces back: it REFLECTS and shows.
The watching eye (見) is the real part - a parent watches closely over their child; the left side (立 over 木) gives only the sound.
It's a horse-word (馬 + the sound 僉); 'test' was only borrowed later - so, TEST.
A bright flower among the grass (艹) is 'brilliant'; 央 gives only the sound (it also spells ENGLAND).
Pull the arrow out and tuck the wound safe in a box: the DOCTOR heals it.
A person stands ready to do their WORK.
Step off the ground and head away: to LEAVE.
Pop it in your mouth to TASTE it and find the MEANING.
Carry a thing across and set it down exactly - to COPY. (Old form: 宀 roof + the sound 舄; the modern 写 hides it.)
Under the roof a child learns to write each LETTER.

examples.gloss: answer or solution to a problem

entries.notes: Bamboo (竹) writing-slips carry your reply; 合 gives only the sound - so, the ANSWER.
A person under the roof with the evening moon out: it is NIGHT.
Stand up and open wide to let the SOUND ring out.
Pour the water right on the spot, pouring in your ATTENTION.
One traditional telling: pick up the broom and head back home = RETURN. (The origin is disputed - see Confidence.)
Open your mouth wide, again and again, to SING.
Bad feelings sit in the heart (心); 亜 gives only the sound - so, BAD.
A little picture tucked inside a box: a MAP.
Walk under the roof until you arrive inside: a ROOM.
One foot, then the other foot: step by step, you WALK.
A little bug carried along inside a puffing sail: the WIND.
Press the threads flat into a thin sheet: PAPER.
Soot from the fire stains it all over: pitch BLACK.
Little sprouts push up toward the warm sun: SPRING.
A big person stands over a blazing fire - the bright color of the flames is RED.
A fresh sprout under a clear sky: cool BLUE.
A big hall where food is served to many people: a large BUILDING.
A roof you come under for shelter: a SHOP or house.
When feelings rise up, they show as the COLOR in your face.

examples.grammar_note: u-verb (Group 1) that looks like a ru-verb (Group 2)

entries.notes: Arms swinging over two fast feet: off you RUN.
Modern-form memory reading: grain (禾) drying by fire (火) at harvest = AUTUMN. (The earliest 秋 was a cricket pictograph.)
Dragging your feet slowly in the heat: SUMMER.
One traditional telling: a young bird flaps its wings over and over to LEARN.
Water spreading wide and far, on and on: the great OCEAN.
Follow the flag with your group down the road: to TRAVEL.
Fitted to your body by hand: the CLOTHES you wear.
A thin curved moon peeks out in the sky: it is EVENING.
Ask a person to lend you something for a while, to BORROW it.
A thick piece with cut lines running through it: that is MEAT.
Hand your money over to someone else for now: to LEND.
A tall roof raised up on solid ground: a grand HALL.
A beak on top, a round body, and tail feathers below: a BIRD.
A warm bowl to turn to at mealtime: cooked RICE.
Push with all your strength to STUDY hard.
You walk slowly through the cold, two icy drops below: WINTER.
The sun sits high over the line at midday: DAYTIME.
The plant part (艹) shows tea leaves; 余 gives only the sound - so, TEA.
The brother who comes lower down in the family line: the YOUNGER BROTHER.
One horn slants off the top of its head: a COW.
A pointed head, a scaly body, and a spread-out tail below: a FISH.
The elder opens his mouth (口) to lead the family's prayer at the altar: the ELDER BROTHER.
Shape memory hook: 犬 looks like 大 'big' with one extra dot (the ear) - but it is really a side-view pictograph of a DOG.
A girl (女) is the meaning; 未 gives only the sound - YOUNGER SISTER (like her sibling 姉).
The grown-up girl who looks after you: your ELDER SISTER.
Named after a great river (see the water on the left): the writing of the people there, the CHINESE characters we call kanji.
Words (言) leaving the mouth = SAY.
Five fingers spreading from a wrist = HAND.
People (人) gathering in clouds (云) = MEET.
A vertical eye with pupil-bars = EYE.
My (厶) grain (禾) = PRIVATE / I.

examples.gloss: entry / entering (often "立入禁止" = no entry)

entries.notes: A person planted on the ground = STAND.
A grid of irrigation channels = RICE PADDY.
Altar (礻) on the earth (土) where people gather = COMPANY / shrine.
A standing tree freshly cut by an axe = NEW.
A flexed arm muscle = POWER.
Walking (辶) with one's head (首) up = ROAD / way.
A square opening = MOUTH.
Mouth (口) over shell-money (貝) - a paid speaker = MEMBER / employee.

examples.gloss: an auspicious day in the traditional Japanese calendar

entries.notes: A woman (女) under a roof (宀) - peaceful and CHEAP.

examples.gloss: footprints (足跡; 跡 written in kana per K-1)

entries.notes: Mouth-shape (口) over stop (止) = FOOT (where you stop).
A cave (穴) of work (工) - empty above = SKY / empty.
Under a roof (广), claim a spot (占) = SHOP.

examples.gloss: old (of things; not a person's age)

entries.notes: Ten (十) generations of stories (口) = OLD.
Net (四) for shell-money (貝) = BUY.
Grass (艹) transforming (化) = FLOWER.
Food (飠) and a yawn (欠) - DRINK to wash it down.
Walking (辶) around (周) the calendar = WEEK.
Horse (馬) measured (尺) - a relay STATION.
Sun (日) + feathers (羽) + bird (隹) - DAY OF THE WEEK named after a celestial body.
A white (白) spot you aim an arrow at -- the TARGET.
A pregnant figure in profile -- your own BODY, yourself.
A mouth (口) giving the OK -- yes, it is POSSIBLE.
